description: FlowMatrix-AI org baseline - safe for all repo types

lockFileMaintenance.description: Renovate's own default for this block is `schedule: ["before 4am on monday"]`, which is NARROWER than the org schedule above and is NOT overridden by it - a top-level schedule does not reach into an update-type block that ships its own. So lock file maintenance only ran when the hosted bot happened to reach a repo before 4am, and was skipped outright on the ~37% of runs that land later in the Monday window. Every one of the 5 scheduled lock-file-maintenance PRs the fleet has ever produced was created before 4am local; none after. This matters more than it looks: lock file maintenance is the ONLY mechanism here that can move a TRANSITIVE pin, so while it was skipped, transitive advisories had no remediation path at all - 12 open Dependabot alerts across 7 repos accumulated behind it, every one of them already satisfiable by the parent's existing range. Pin the schedule to the org window explicitly so it stops inheriting the narrower default. Related: #27 (Monday-only scheduling problems generally).

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Renovate's built-in default for this block sets groupName: null, which OVERRIDES any groupName a packageRules entry would otherwise apply. A security update is therefore deliberately un-grouped - fine for a self-contained dependency, actively harmful for an ecosystem whose packages must move together. Re-establish grouping for those ecosystems here. The outer groupName stays null so unrelated security fixes are still not batched; schedule and minimumReleaseAge are pinned to Renovate's vulnerabilityAlerts defaults explicitly so a security fix is never held by the Monday schedule or the 3-day soak above. Rule of thumb: if packages are grouped because a partial update breaks the build, that grouping MUST be repeated here. See #31.

packageRules.description: Tailwind must move as a set under a security advisory too. @tailwindcss/postcss and @tailwindcss/vite each carry an EXACT `tailwindcss` dependency (4.3.3 depends on tailwindcss 4.3.3, not a range), so a lone `tailwindcss` bump desyncs the tree rather than upgrading it. Same shape as the astro rule below.

Astro must move as a set under a security advisory too. On 2026-07/08 three repos took a lone `astro` 6->7 security bump with no @astrojs/* companions; the adapter peers a specific astro major, so all three failed on arrival and sat red for a month while six XSS advisories stayed open. Distinct group name from the routine `astro` group so a security remediation is never entangled with a pending routine major.
Cloudflare must move as a set under a security advisory too -- wrangler peers @cloudflare/workers-types across a major boundary. Same shape as the astro and tailwind rules.

Route the PUBLIC @flowmatrix-ai packages at npmjs. Every other package in the scope (the eight checkout-*, site-generator) is GitHub-Packages-only and 404s on npmjs, which is why the scope-wide npmrc above stays pointed there. GitHub Packages answers 401 to an unauthenticated reader even for these, so a Renovate lookup without a token finds nothing and proposes no update - the failure mode is silence, not an error. Verified 2026-08-27 by unauthenticated GET: site-components/site-config/site-functions => 200 on npmjs; brand, site-generator and every checkout-* => 404; all thirteen => 401 on GitHub Packages. brand joined the npmjs side on 2026-08-31 (brand#92) - DO NOT MERGE THIS AHEAD OF THAT PUBLISH, or brand lookups 404 and Renovate silently stops offering brand updates fleet-wide. NOTE: registryUrls governs version LOOKUP only - it does NOT change the resolved URLs Renovate writes into a regenerated lockfile. That is the npmrc's job, which is why migrated sites extend the site-npmjs preset instead. First in the list so it only sets a registry and leaves the automerge rules below to decide merging.

Group the astro framework with its adapters and integrations across ALL update types, so a major lands as one coherent PR. The adapter peers a specific astro major (@astrojs/cloudflare 13 peers astro ^6, 14 peers astro ^7), so a partial bump leaves the set incompatible and the build fails - `Missing field moduleType` on the Cloudflare stack, a rolldown binding error elsewhere. marketing-site.json carries its own copy of this rule because it must also set automerge and must win over that preset's `npm non-major` group; this one exists so the 52 repos on the bare default preset are covered too. No automerge key here: default.json never automerges anything above a patch. See checkout-site-engine#154.

Group wrangler with the @cloudflare packages, and do NOT separate majors. wrangler declares a peer on @cloudflare/workers-types and crossed a workers-types MAJOR boundary inside its own MINOR range: 4.102.0 peers ^4.20260617.1, 4.125.0 peers ^5.20260820.1, 4.127.0 peers ^5.20260826.1. So the wrangler half of the move is non-major while the workers-types half is a major. separateMajorMinor defaults to true, so a groupName alone would still put them in two branches -- which is exactly what happened: happy-house-bathrooms#45 carried wrangler and left workers-types on 4.x, #57 carried workers-types and left wrangler behind, and both sat red for weeks. Neither was buildable: npm cannot resolve the peer conflict, so Renovate could not regenerate the lockfile either (renovate/artifacts "Artifact file update failure"), and CI reported a misleading `npm ci` EUSAGE lockfile mismatch. separateMajorMinor:false is the part that actually fixes it.
Conservative automerge: digest/pin updates for language + CI-action managers only. Terraform/Docker/custom (i.e. infra) are excluded so they stay manual. Gated by required ok + gitleaks checks.
Conservative automerge: stable (>=1.0.0) patch updates for language + CI-action managers only. Terraform/Docker/custom excluded; minors/majors stay manual.

Hold TypeScript MAJOR behind Dependency-Dashboard approval instead of auto-opening a PR. TS7 (Go-native, GA 2026-07-08) is a native compiler that does not yet ship the programmatic API `astro check` loads, so `@astrojs/check` refuses it outright: "The TypeScript module loaded (found 7.0.2) does not expose the programmatic API that `astro check` relies on ... run `astro check` with a TypeScript version that still provides it (6.x)" (flowmatrixai-org#30, 2026-08-31). It is not only an Astro problem: checkout-site-engine#178 failed in the plain workspace typecheck with TS2591/TS2304 on the @types/node globals, and client-portal#109 died inside its own build with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Cjs')`. So there are at least three independent blockers, and widening the @astrojs/check peer range will not be enough on its own. THIS RULE LIVED ONLY IN marketing-site.json UNTIL 2026-08-31, which meant every repo on the bare default preset kept opening a TS7 PR that cannot pass -- five of them in one Renovate run (client-portal, creative-engine, flowmatrixai-org, marketing-site-engine, site-flowmatrixai-main). Dashboard approval keeps the major VISIBLE and one-click (never silently dropped, as allowedVersions would), so it is not forgotten: tick the box to re-test once the ecosystem catches up. TS minor/patch still auto-flow.

Do not let Renovate manage engines.npm. Renovate proposes npm LATEST for that field (12.0.2 today), but npm ships bundled with node and no node ships one that far ahead -- node 24.19.0 ships npm 11.17.0 -- so the proposed engines pair is unsatisfiable. Where a repo enforces it the build dies outright (the-hunt-advisory-site#53: EBADENGINE on every job including Vercel, because that repo sets engine-strict=true deliberately -- npm <11.6 silently strips the `libc` field from package-lock.json). Where it is not enforced the incoherence is simply invisible: as of 2026-08-28 four repos declared npm >=12.0.2 and one >=11.19.0 on node that ships 11.17.0, all green. An npm floor is a policy pin about a known bug, so it is set by hand. engines.node is deliberately still managed -- only npm is held.
